newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Clinton arrives in Canberra, trade to dominate talk.
newsitem.headline: Clinton arrives in Canberra, trade to dominate talk.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton arrived in Canberra on Wednesday for what is likely to be the only real working day of his five-day visit to Australia.

Clinton, accompanied by wife Hillary, arrived in the Australian capital after a 30-minute flight from Sydney aboard a U.S. Air Force Boeing 747 after a last minute switch of aircraft caused by an apparent mechanical fault.
Security officials at Sydney Airport confirmed there had been a mechanical problem with the Boeing 707 that had been scheduled to make the flight but would not give details.

Clinton, who arrived in Sydney on Tuesday night, was due to lay a wreath at the Australian War Memorial, meet Prime Minister John Howard and Opposition Leader Kim Beazley, hold a news conference and address a joint sitting of Parliament before returning to Sydney on Wednesday evening for a harbour cruise.
The low-key visit is largely seen as a warm-up for Clinton's attendance at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum in the Philippines next week.
Apart from extolling U.S.-Australia ties, Clinton is expected to use his speech to reassert the U.S. commitment to Asia and his wish for deeper engagement with China.

But the president can expect some tough talk from Howard on U.S. trade policies during their one-hour meeting, including the touchy issue of U.S. agricultural subsidies which Australia claims threaten its traditional markets.
As if to underscore the point, Clinton was to be met at the airport by Australian Trade Minister Tim Fischer, who is also deputy prime minister.
Howard has tried to boost Australia's ties with the United States, which he says were neglected under his predecessor Paul Keating whose leadership was marked by a desire to embrace Asia.
Apart from a speech to the Australian people from a site near the Sydney Opera House on Thursday, Clinton's schedule is largely free, allowing him time for at least one game of golf.
Australia's world number one Greg Norman and rising U.S. star Tiger Woods, both playing in a Sydney tournament, are obvious potential partners.
On Thursday evening, the Clintons fly off to the tropical resort of Port Douglas on the Great Barrier Reef for two days of swimming, snorkelling and, probably, more golf.
The president and his entourage leave Sydney on Saturday for the Philippines, where he will join a summit meeting of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum on Monday.
